up.note:
Take $w^x$ to be the indicator of a minimal certificate for $x$. If
$f(x)\ne f(y)$ then the two certificates must disagree on some queried
coordinate -- otherwise they would be jointly satisfiable and the value
undetermined -- so $\sum_{i:x_i\ne y_i} w^x_i w^y_i \ge 1$, and
$\sum_i w^x_i = \mathrm{C}_x(f)$. Nothing here needs $f$ total.

Upper bounds — holds for every partial

  • \(\mathrm{EC}(f) \le \mathrm{C}(f)\)
    GJKKLSSV17
    Take $w^x$ to be the indicator of a minimal certificate for $x$. If $f(x)\ne f(y)$ then the two certificates must disagree on some queried coordinate -- otherwise they would be jointly satisfiable and the value undetermined -- so $\sum_{i:x_i\ne y_i} w^x_i w^y_i \ge 1$, and $\sum_i w^x_i = \mathrm{C}_x(f)$. Nothing here needs $f$ total.

Recorded because without it the $\mathrm{EC}$ row has no upper bound at all: the measure was introduced for the inequalities that bound $\mathrm{R}_0$ from below, and $\mathrm{EC} \le \mathrm{R}_0 = O(\mathrm{EC}^2)$ [GJKKLSSV17] reaches nothing else. Through $\mathrm{C}$ the row inherits the rest of the zoo, and the two routes agree: $\mathrm{EC}\le\mathrm{C}\le\mathrm{R}_0$.

see also: \(\mathrm{EC}(f)\), \(\mathrm{C}(f)\), \(\mathrm{FC}(f)\), \(\mathrm{fbs}(f)\), \(\mathrm{R}_{0}(f)\) data/relations/10-new-measures.yaml

lo.note:
A single character has sparsity $1$ and $\mathrm{osss} = 1$: the two agree, but neither
grows, so this witnesses no exponent. No function in the zoo has $\mathrm{osss}$ growing
while $\mathrm{spar}$ stays bounded -- indeed $\mathrm{spar}(f) = O(1)$ forces $f$ to be a
constant-size combination of characters, and $\mathrm{osss}$ is then bounded too.
